review_rationale: batch116: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...), plus a closeout re-verification. Reviewer read all 21 base units in the original PDF and verified the titles from the source as Purpose and form of the SELECT RANK construct, Execution of the SELECT RANK construct, Attributes of a SELECT RANK associate name, and Examples of the SELECT RANK construct. Verified 21 base / 47 fine units, 21 requirements and 63 facets, all pending, and confirmed the accounting that only 10 base units are newly accounted because the eleven numbered items R1150 through R1153 and C1155 through C1161 were already counted. The reviewer independently confirmed that none of those numbered rules has pre-existing cases under tests, which matters because registering a numbered rule that already has legacy fixtures structurally forces binding them and would make a source packet claim execution credit without fixture review. The rank-matching rules were derived independently from the source before comparison, covering which RANK guard matches which selector rank, the assumed-size and default cases, that at most one block is selected, and the precedence when several guards could match. Both permissions were adjudicated: the 11.1.10.1 p3 latitude for a rank value greater than the maximum possible rank, whose block never executes, and the 11.1.10.2 p2 internal branch to END SELECT, whose only wording also supplies the paired outside-branch restriction. The packet was blocked on its first pass with one finding, closed and re-verified. C11SRR-001 observed that the first sentence of C1161 carries two distinct obligations, not one: a named SELECT RANK construct's END SELECT statement shall specify a construct name, and that name shall be the same. The packet had a wrong-name negative and the reverse unnamed-construct-with-named-END negative, but no facet for a named SELECT RANK with an unnamed END SELECT, leaving a distinct prohibition without an oracle row. The correction added named-select-rank-unnamed-end-rejected with a control differing only by the presence of the END name, taking the packet from 62 to 63 facets with requirements unchanged. Because the defect was a compound shall sentence whose second obligation was missed, a sweep of the whole scope was required and then re-derived from the source by the reviewer: C1155 has two obligations covered by three legitimate facets, C1156 and C1157 one each, C1158, C1159 and C1160 two each, C1161 three now covered, and R1150 through R1153 carry production alternatives with no omitted compound constraint. The ownership boundary against 11.1.3.3 was checked in both directions, with this packet owning SELECT RANK-specific association, rank matching, rank and bounds, and ALLOCATABLE, POINTER and TARGET inheritance, while 11.1.3.3 retains the general associate-name attributes. Assumed-rank dependencies on unregistered Clause 15 are flagged explicitly. Final decision: accept, no blocking findings. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
